title: The Sh2-54 nebula in the infrared with VISTA
caption: The Sh2-54 nebula, imaged by ESO's VISTA telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Stars shine through the clouds of the Sh2-54 nebula in this infrared view. It was taken with ESO's VISTA telescope at Paranal Observatory in Chile.

The Sh2-54 nebula shows just how much the kind of light matters. In visible light, the dust and gas of Sh2-54 are obvious. In infrared light those clouds become much less noticeable, and the light of stars behind the nebula pierces through.

This happens because infrared light has longer wavelengths than visible light and passes through dust far more easily. Astronomers use this to look inside and behind dusty regions, spotting stars that would otherwise be hidden. Comparing infrared and visible views of the same nebula helps them build a fuller picture of what the cloud contains.

understand.summary: VISTA's VIRCAM camera imaged the nebula in near-infrared light through J, H and Ks filters. The colour mapping isn't published.
